title.narrative: Enhancing the integrated life-saving SRH and GBV services for flood affected populations in Borno State.

description.narrative: This project will seek to provide and increase access to sexual and reproductive health (SRH), and gender-based violence (GBV) prevention and response services, as well as Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) services to the flood affected populations in Borno State, Northeast Nigeria. The proposed activities under this call responds to the CERR’s life-saving criteria as they focus on;- Provision of integrated SRH/GBV services through the camp-based health facilities, as well as the established women and girls’ safe spaces, and referral for higher level care. - Provision of holistic GBV response services through One Stop Service Center. - Procurement of medical commodities including the clean delivery kits to support the SRH/GBV service delivery - Procurement of dignity kits including the menstrual hygiene items and distribution to the women and girls of reproductive age. - Dissemination of key SRH and GBV messages through community outreaches and linkages with the service providers. Specifically, UNFPA will work with the existing implementing partners (IPs) to deliver life-saving services. UNFPA’s frontline workers including the midwives and GBV case workers will be deployed through the IPs to deliver life-saving minimum initial service package for SRH that cover the aspect of the clinical management of rape (CMR) while UNFPA will continue to provide technical support and medical commodities. The frontline workers will engage with the women and girls in the camps to provide antenatal care, delivery, postnatal care, CMR, family planning and referral for emergency obstetric care services. Additionally, pregnant women will also be reached through the distribution of clean delivery kits to improve the hygienic conditions at birth; information related to birth planning and referral points will be provided at distribution. Moreover, the project will facilitate increased access to GBV response services and referral, and ensure GBV risk mitigation through safety audits and awareness-raising activities. Those who experience displacement because of the devastating floods are often distressed and have been exposed to traumatic events. Therefore, the aspect of MHPSS will also be integrated in both SRH and GBV service provision while also taking into consideration the specific needs of the most vulnerable population, such as persons living with disability (PLWD) and adolescent girls. Dignity kit distribution will provide an opportunity for awareness raising on key protection risks, sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), GBV risk mitigation measures and the availability of response services.
